title: Docs Viewer Search Tokenizer
summary: Durable normalization and term-recognition contract shared by Docs Viewer index generation and browser queries.
content_html:
Docs Viewer Search Tokenizer

Docs Viewer index generation and browser queries use the same deterministic term contract. Python generation is implemented in docs-viewer/build/build_search.py; browser query normalization is implemented in site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-search.js. One shared fixture proves parity.

Term Contract

For each value selected by a scope's field policy, the tokenizer:

  1. applies Unicode NFKC normalization and lowercase comparison;
  2. recognizes prose words and technical compounds before discarding punctuation;
  3. retains the normalized complete compound and useful components split on underscore, hyphen, dot, and camel-case boundaries;
  4. retains mixed alphabetic/numeric identifiers such as r2, h1, and sm-1.0;
  5. omits numeric-only values, one-character values, complete immutable document IDs, exact 64-character hexadecimal digests, URLs, paths, markup spans, and file-extension-only components;
  6. removes the fixed minimal stop-word list; and
  7. deduplicates terms before the index adds a document position to one field posting list.

Examples:

authored or queried text terms
Full-text search full-text, full, text, search
docs_subscope docs_subscope, docs, subscope
DOCS_VIEWER_BASE_URL docs_viewer_base_url, docs, viewer, base, url
handleEditMetadataSave handleeditmetadatasave, handle, edit, metadata, save
build_search.py build_search.py, build, search
SM-1.0 sm-1.0, sm
2026 omitted
d-20260715-084611-c2fa6f omitted
a 64-character SHA-256 value omitted

The fixed stop words are a, an, and, are, as, at, be, by, for, from, in, is, it, of, on, or, that, the, to, and with. Technical lifecycle words such as before, after, and while remain searchable. Terms are not removed merely because they occur in many documents.

Query Semantics

Queries use the same term derivation as indexed content. A query reduced entirely to excluded or stop-word terms returns no result. At three or more characters, a query term also matches indexed terms beginning with that term. Multi-term queries require every normalized query term to match the same document.

Exact structural fields are separate from ordinary term derivation. A metadata-only scope can explicitly enable exact identity or last_updated; Studio does not enable either field.

Change Rule

Tokenizer behavior is intentionally small: no stemming, synonyms, spelling correction, language detection, or corpus-derived stop words. A change must update Python generation, browser JavaScript, and the shared tokenizer fixture together, then rebuild affected indexes. Scope-specific vocabulary rules or a second tokenizer are not allowed. Corpus frequency may inform the shared relevance score without removing terms or changing their tokenisation.

Docs Viewer Search Index owns the payload and field boundary. Docs Viewer Search Relevance owns proposed corpus-adaptive weighting and evidence-led language extensions. DSI-1 — Docs Viewer Search Index v2 Delivery and SM-1 — Studio Full-Text Search Delivery retain implementation evidence.
